brief.industry_meta: Marketing Technology · Customer Data Platform / AI Decisioning
brief.deck: San Francisco marketing-data company Hightouch announced a $150M Series D at a $2.75B valuation on 29 April 2026, led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives' growth arm and Bain Capital Ventures, more than doubling its price in fourteen months. Its buyers are chief marketing officers, the audience paddock hospitality was built for.
brief.the_case_p1: Hightouch announced on 29 April that it had raised $150M in a Series D led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Bain Capital Ventures at a $2.75B valuation, with Iconiq, Sapphire Ventures, Amplify, Y Combinator and TD7, The Trade Desk's venture arm, participating; total funding is about $322M. Hightouch says revenue has grown more than 100% in each of the past two years, and names Domino's, PetSmart, DraftKings, Ramp and Whoop among customers. Its Series C, $80M at $1.2B led by Sapphire, closed in February 2025.
brief.the_case_p2: The product is a marketing data layer that reads a company's warehouse and pushes audiences to advertising, email and CRM tools, with AI agents deciding what each customer sees next. It is bought by marketing leaders, which makes the paddock a sales floor, not a billboard. Gartner named Hightouch a Leader in its 2025 Magic Quadrant for customer data platforms in January, and no team on the grid carries a partner in the category.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round was announced on 29 April; budgets reset in the quarter after a raise, and Hightouch is spending on category leadership. The European rounds from Monaco, then the US GP and Las Vegas, fall inside the window, and teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief.why_team_para: McLaren carries the longest technology roster in the sponsor table, and its fan-data lane has just opened: Salesforce, whose platform ran McLaren's fan-relationship programme, has departed, while Google Cloud has joined. Alteryx and Splunk cover analytics and observability; nothing on the roster activates fan data into media, email and the store. Hightouch fills that slot, with a warehouse-side partner already in place.
brief.value_section_label: VALUE TO MCLAREN MASTERCARD F1 TEAM
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Hightouch as the activation layer on McLaren's fan data: audiences built from ticketing, store, app and content behaviour in the team's warehouse, pushed to paid media, email and the McLaren store, with AI decisioning choosing the next offer for each fan. The team gets a measured lift in fan revenue; Hightouch gets a reference customer and a paddock full of chief marketing officers at the US GP and Las Vegas.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Marketing Data Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, covering the next raise and a probable listing window. Estimated $2-4M a year, part in kind via platform licence and services. Scope: mirror or engine-cover placement, a fan-data activation programme with McLaren's digital team, CMO hospitality at the US rounds, and a co-authored annual fan-data report.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Gupta co-founded Hightouch in 2018 and shares the CEO role with Tejas Manohar; a Wharton graduate and former Bessemer investor, he fronts the raises. Path: Tejas Manohar, Co-Founder & Co-CEO; Cherry Miao, CFO; Brian Kotlyar, VP Marketing & Growth. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the buyer, not the badge.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Kashish, your buyers are CMOs, and every one of them passes through a Formula 1 paddock. McLaren's fan-data lane opened when Salesforce left, and Google Cloud just arrived. 25 minutes before Monaco to see the numbers?”
score_cells: Round announced 29 Apr; European rounds and two US races ahead.
$2.75B valuation; $322M raised; a mid-tier partner budget.
B2B martech; the paddock is where its buyers are.
No listing date; category leadership is the only clock.
MODE A: fan-data activation on a warehouse the team runs.
risks: Freshworks and Medallia sit on McLaren's roster in customer software; a marketing-data partner must be scoped so neither reads it as a rival.
Define the category as warehouse-native fan-data activation; get written non-conflict from McLaren before signing.
At $2.75B and $322M raised, Hightouch is a mid-tier partner on the grid's longest technology roster; car visibility will be modest.
Buy the workstream and the hospitality, not the livery; measure the deal on pipeline from the paddock.
brief.bottom_line: A $150M Series D at $2.75B, revenue more than doubling for two years and a customer list that includes Whoop and DraftKings put Hightouch at peak brand-investment authority. McLaren's fan-data lane opened when Salesforce departed, and the buyers Hightouch needs are already in the paddock.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: Hightouch announced on 29 April 2026 a $150M Series D led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Bain Capital Ventures at a $2.75B valuation, with Iconiq, Sapphire Ventures, Amplify Partners, Y Combinator and TD7, The Trade Desk's venture arm, participating. Total funding is about $322M across six rounds. The release is the company's own, so the figures are announced, not reported.

why_now.label: Price more than doubled
why_now.text: The Series C of February 2025, $80M led by Sapphire Ventures, valued Hightouch at $1.2B. Fourteen months later the Series D priced it at $2.75B. Hightouch says revenue has grown more than 100% in each of the past two years; no revenue figure is public and none is used here.

why_now.label: Category leadership is being bought
why_now.text: Gartner named Hightouch a Leader in the 2025 Magic Quadrant for Customer Data Platforms (announced 29 January 2026). The company is investing to hold that position against Salesforce, Adobe and the warehouse vendors, and its buyers, chief marketing officers, are the people a Formula 1 partnership puts in a room.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: From the 5 May row date the European rounds run from Monaco to Monza; the US GP and Las Vegas fall in the last quarter of the calendar. Teams close 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter, so a conversation opened in May can be announced at a US round and activated in full for 2027.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: McLaren's technology roster is the longest in the sponsor table: Google Cloud, Dell, Cisco, Splunk, Alteryx, Smartsheet, Medallia, Dropbox, Workday, Freshworks, Okta, Groq, Gemini and Rubrik. Salesforce, whose platform ran McLaren's fan-relationship programme, has departed. Nothing on the roster activates fan data into media, email and the store: Official Marketing Data Partner is a clean designation.

why_team.label: A stack to plug into
why_team.text: Hightouch reads a company's cloud data warehouse rather than copying the data into its own system; Google Cloud joined McLaren's roster this season, giving the programme a warehouse-side partner already in place.

why_team.label: A team that will use the product
why_team.text: McLaren's commercial machine is the most visible on the grid: a global fan base, a large store and a hospitality programme that is itself a marketing operation. Fan-data activation is consumed by the team's digital and commercial staff every week, which is what separates a technology partner from a logo.

why_team.label: The buyer audience
why_team.text: Hightouch sells to chief marketing officers. McLaren's partners are largely enterprise brands whose CMOs attend the races; a seat at the Paddock Club at the US GP and Las Vegas is a sales floor for Hightouch as much as a brand placement.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Audiences built from ticketing, store, app and content behaviour in McLaren's warehouse, pushed to paid media, email and the McLaren store, with AI decisioning choosing the next offer for each fan and measuring lift. The team funds no new data platform; Hightouch supplies the activation layer and the services to run it.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: A measured increase in fan revenue per head across store, tickets and hospitality, reported quarterly, and a partner whose guest list is chief marketing officers, the audience McLaren's other B2B partners want in the suite.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: A co-authored annual fan-data report on how a Formula 1 team markets to its fans, McLaren as a named reference customer for Hightouch's enterprise sales, and engineering-to-marketing content that fits the team's technology positioning.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Marketing Data Partner designation, mirror or engine-cover placement, integration rights across McLaren's fan-data estate, US-round hospitality, and driver access for Hightouch's customer events.

ruled_out.reason: Oracle is title partner and sells its own customer-data and marketing cloud; direct conflict.
Confluent (data streaming) and RebelDot (software) crowd the data lane.
Sprinklr and MNTN departed within the last 12 months and Avature and IndraMind joined; a marketing-software lane recently vacated and re-filled.
TikTok, Cognizant and ServiceNow occupy the marketing-platform and enterprise-software positions.
SAP, Solera, TeamViewer, Microsoft and Meta AI crowd enterprise software and AI.
Infobip, a customer-engagement platform, is a team partner; adjacent conflict.
Open but not chosen: Whoop, a Hightouch customer, is a Ferrari partner, which is a warm introduction rather than a lane; Ferrari's technology roster is HP-led and the fan-data story is weaker.

ruled_out.team: Atlassian Williams Racing · Audi F1 Team · Cadillac F1 Team
ruled_out.reason: Open but not chosen: none carries the Salesforce-vacated, Google Cloud-backed fan-data setup that makes McLaren the natural home.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Kashish Gupta and Tejas Manohar before Monaco to test appetite, agree how a fan-data activation programme would be measured, and size an Official Marketing Data Partner entry against McLaren's 2027 roster.

## The trigger

Company-announced: Hightouch's own release on BusinessWire, "Hightouch Raises $150 Million to Reinvent How Marketing Works Using AI". The BusinessWire URL carries 27 April; the trade coverage (Retail Technology Innovation Hub, citybiz, Pulse 2.0) and the search summary of the release date it 29 April 2026, which the brief uses; Built In San Francisco ran it on 30 April. Either date is inside the 90-day window of the 5 May row. $150M Series D, $2.75B valuation, led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Bain Capital Ventures.

## Screen-outs and things not claimed

- **No revenue figure**: Hightouch says growth exceeded 100% in each of the past two years; no absolute figure is public and none is used.
- **Product integration with McLaren's stack is not claimed as fact.** Google Cloud's presence on the roster comes from the sponsor table; the copy says it gives the programme a warehouse-side partner, not that McLaren's warehouse runs on it. Hightouch's most common data sources were not verified this session and are not named.
- **McLaren fan-base, store and hospitality figures** are not quantified: none were sourced.
- **Deal size ($2-4M a year) is an ESTIMATE**, labelled as such.
- **The Snowflake partner-of-the-year award (June 2026)** post-dates the row and is left out.
- **Ramp**, a named Hightouch customer, is on 1440's approached list (`data/approached.json`); it is mentioned only as a customer, not as a route in.
- **Score 73, not the row's 87:** capacity is 15 (a $2.75B company with $322M raised is a mid-tier partner) and brand fit 13 (B2B martech). The case rests on the buyer audience and a real Mode A workstream.

## Decision path

Kashish Gupta, Co-Founder & Co-CEO (fronts the raises), with Tejas Manohar, Co-Founder & Co-CEO. Path: Cherry Miao, CFO; Brian Kotlyar, VP Marketing & Growth. **No chief marketing officer is listed** (Craft executive listing, cross-checked with Contrary Research and the release). The company's own leadership page could not be opened from the sandbox.

## Leadership ties

No F1/FE ecosystem tie found for Gupta, Manohar, Curl, Miao or Kotlyar after checking; no motorsport customer case study found. `leadership_ties`: none found.

## Team choice

McLaren over Williams, Audi, Cadillac and Ferrari (all open). McLaren is the only roster where a customer-data platform (Salesforce) has just departed and a cloud partner (Google Cloud) has just joined, and its commercial programme is the most visible on the grid. Adjacent partners (Freshworks, Medallia) are the first risk and are named.
